stages.name: Opening & Chapter 1
stages.why: The opening missions are mandatory and teach the movement, combat and map systems used by every later stage. There is nothing to gain by leaving the story path yet.
stages.save: Autosave is enough; make one manual save before the first stranger marker appears.

stages.name: Chapter 2 story
stages.why: Chapter 2 continues the required path and introduces the mission types that recur later. Clear it before world activities so the map has more of its tools unlocked.
stages.save: Manual save on the Chapter 2 checkpoint; keep it for a strand replay.

stages.name: Chapter 3 story
stages.why: Three mission trophies sit close together here. Taking them in story order avoids replaying a heist for one missed results screen.
stages.save: Manual save before The Cartel Heist if you intend to replay for a clean result.

stages.name: Chapter 4 story
stages.why: The chapter ends on a set-piece mission. Finish it in one sitting so the closing cutscene and results screen are not interrupted.
stages.save: Manual save before Operation Savage Glory.

stages.name: Finale & stranger strands
stages.why: Clear the coral-flagged jobs before the finale, then finish the story. The last main mission is the point of no return for several stranger chains and partner jobs.
stages.save: Manual save before the final mission and before each strand’s last job.

stages.name: Free-roam one-offs
stages.window: Open world, any chapter after the tutorial
stages.why: These are single actions and short activities. Most are repeatable or retryable, so they cost little time and can be cleared between story missions.
stages.save: Only the coral-flagged catches need a manual save.

stages.name: Long-haul completions
stages.window: Open world, best after the map is fully open
stages.why: Counts such as 250 stunts and 42 shooting ranges are faster with the whole map available. Doing them after the story avoids re-crossing locked districts.
stages.save: Save before a long session; progress is cumulative.

stages.name: 100% completion
stages.why: A Long Road is the capstone. Most earlier trophies feed the completion checklist, so the final percentage is cheapest once stages 06 and 07 are done.
stages.save: Keep one manual save before the last few percentage points.

stages.name: Platinum
stages.why: Vice Got a Price! has no separate task. It pops when the other 54 trophies are on the profile, so it closes the table rather than opening a new lane.
stages.save: No save needed; sync the trophy list if the pop is delayed.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the completion reward, not a separate task. It unlocks the moment the other 54 trophies are on your profile, so the practical plan is to work stages 01–08 and leave this lane empty. Do not start a second playthrough for it, and do not chase online substitutes. If the pop is delayed, sync the console and reopen the trophy app before doing anything destructive.
trophies.short: The platinum: earn the other 54 trophies and it unlocks on its own.

steps.text: Treat the platinum as the remainder: earn the other 54 first.
Finish the stranger strands and the 100% checklist before the final cleanup.
If the pop is late, sync the console and reopen the trophy app.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so it cannot be skipped on a normal run. Follow the story marker until the final objective and let the closing scene play out instead of quitting early; the trophy is awarded on the results screen. If you are replaying for cleanup, use mission replay rather than starting a new save. No collectible or side activity is needed. The prologue autosave is the clean replay point; mission replay also works if the results screen was skipped [4].
trophies.short: Finish the opening mission Gone Fishing.

steps.text: Start the campaign and follow the story marker into Gone Fishing.
Complete the last objective and watch the closing cutscene through to the results screen.
Keep the autosave from the prologue; it is the cleanest replay point.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter completion follows the story path, not the completion percentage. Keep taking main missions until the Chapter 1 wrap screen appears; side content can wait because the chapter does not close while you are inside it. Make a manual save at the boundary for the stranger strands later. This trophy itself cannot be lost.
trophies.short: Complete every Chapter 1 story mission.

steps.text: Take every main-story mission in Chapter 1 in the order the game offers them.
Play through the chapter wrap and let the results screen appear.
Make a manual save after the wrap before moving into Chapter 2.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is required story progress. Follow the main mission chain until the chapter-complete screen; the trophy is not tied to optional jobs or collectibles. A manual save at the end of the chapter is worth keeping for the stranger strands that close later. There is no way to lock yourself out of this bronze. Practical note: the Chapter 2 results screen is the checkpoint to bank; keep that manual save rather than a mid-mission autosave [4][6].
trophies.short: Complete Chapter 2 of the main story.

steps.text: Continue the main mission chain through Chapter 2.
Complete the final chapter mission and let the results screen appear.
Keep a manual save at the chapter boundary for later strand cleanup.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 story missions sit on the required path. Follow the main marker through the chapter until the wrap screen appears, and do not leave the final mission midway through the closing scene. The chapter-internal heist and VCIA missions have their own trophies, so this one usually arrives last. A boundary save is useful for the remaining side content.
trophies.short: Complete Chapter 3 of the main story.

steps.text: Play the Chapter 3 main missions in story order.
Finish the last chapter mission and watch the wrap screen.
Save at the boundary before starting the next chapter.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is mandatory story content. Continue the main mission chain and let the final chapter mission and its results screen finish. The chapter trophy is separate from the Operation Savage Glory mission trophy, so both can appear in the same session. Keep a manual save at the boundary for the stranger strands.
trophies.short: Complete Chapter 4 of the main story.

steps.text: Follow the Chapter 4 main chain to its final mission.
Finish the mission and let the chapter wrap screen appear.
Manual-save at the boundary before the finale stage.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This is the main-story finale and one of the two gold trophies. Play the last mission through its closing sequence without quitting, because the award lands after the final cutscene. Clear the coral-flagged stranger strands before starting it; the finale is the point of no return for several of them. Keep a manual save before the mission so a failed objective does not replay the whole chain. The finale’s results screen is the trigger, so let the credits sequence settle before closing the application [4][6].
trophies.short: Finish the final main-story mission for a gold trophy.

steps.text: Clear the coral-flagged stranger strands before starting the final mission.
Play the finale through the last objective and the closing cutscene.
Let the results screen finish and confirm the gold trophy.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission, not a world activity. Follow the main mission marker until Breakfast Run appears and play it to the end. The trophy is awarded at the results screen, so do not quit after the last objective. Mission replay is available if you missed the screen. Breakfast Run appears in the Chapter 2 chain before the chapter-complete award; treat its results screen as the trigger [5].
trophies.short: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run.

steps.text: Reach Breakfast Run through the Chapter 2 main chain.
Complete its objectives and let the results screen appear.
Replay from the pause menu if the award did not register.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story mission with a mission-specific trophy. Play it as part of the Chapter 3 chain and finish every objective before leaving the area. The award is checked on the results screen, not when the vault opens. If you are cleaning up later, use mission replay rather than a new save. The vault objective can show complete before the escape is registered; stay in the mission until the results screen appears [5].
trophies.short: Complete The Cartel Heist.

steps.text: Start The Cartel Heist from the Chapter 3 main chain.
Finish the heist objectives and the escape sequence.
Wait for the results screen before quitting.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child’s Play is a required Chapter 2 mission. Follow the main marker, complete the mission objectives and let the closing scene finish. The trophy is separate from the Chapter 2 completion trophy and may appear earlier. There is no optional step or collectible involved. The mission unlocks inside Chapter 2 before the chapter-complete trophy, so do not assume the chapter award covers it [4].
trophies.short: Complete the story mission Child's Play.

steps.text: Play Child’s Play as part of the Chapter 2 story chain.
Complete the last objective and let the results screen appear.
No side activity is required for this award.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named Chapter 3 mission, not a repeatable activity. Take it from the main story chain and finish the mission through its closing scene. The trophy is awarded on the results screen. If the mission is already complete, replay it from the pause menu for a clean result. Expect a vehicle escape after the venue objective; park a fast car before the final approach so the results screen is not delayed [5].
trophies.short: Complete the story mission Headliners.

steps.text: Reach Headliners through the Chapter 3 main chain.
Complete its objectives and escape sequence.
Let the results screen finish before leaving.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a Chapter 3 story mission. Follow the main chain until it appears, then play every objective through to the end. The airport setting can make the escape messy, so keep a fast vehicle nearby. The trophy is checked at the results screen, not when the target goes down. The airport escape is the risky part; leave a fast vehicle outside the terminal instead of relying on a spawned one [5].
trophies.short: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown.

steps.text: Start VCIA Takedown from the Chapter 3 story chain.
Complete the assault and the escape without leaving the mission area.
Wait for the results screen and the trophy pop.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory closes Chapter 4 and has its own mission trophy. Play the mission through the final set-piece and let the results screen appear; quitting during the closing scene can lose the award. A manual save before the mission is useful if you want a cleaner replay. The chapter trophy may pop in the same session. The set-piece has a short vehicle section after the main objective; keep the escape route clear rather than quitting at the cutscene [6].
trophies.short: Complete Operation Savage Glory.

steps.text: Start Operation Savage Glory from the Chapter 4 chain.
Finish the set-piece and the closing sequence.
Let the results screen appear before quitting.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Treat 100% as the final audit, not a grind to start early. After the campaign, open the in-game completion checklist and read every remaining line before touching the map. Many of the other trophies feed the same percentage, so clearing stages 06 and 07 first makes the last pass shorter. The game’s own checklist is the only counter that matters. The in-game checklist is the only counter that matters; compare each remaining line with the trophy list before starting a long grind [4].
trophies.short: Reach 100% completion for a gold trophy.

steps.text: Finish the campaign and open the in-game completion checklist.
Clear the collectible and activity lines before the long counts.
Mop up the last percentage points and confirm the checklist reads 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunt counts come from free-roam jumps, rolls and tricks rather than story set pieces. Pick a stretch of road with repeatable ramps and run it in short loops; the activity screen shows the running total. Motorcycles make the roll timing easier, but a failed landing still costs time. There is no time limit, so break it into sessions of twenty-five.
trophies.short: Complete 250 stunts in free roam.

steps.text: Find a repeatable ramp or stunt route in free roam.
Run the route in short loops and check the activity counter.
Repeat until the counter reaches 250 stunts.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: This asks for coverage, not mastery. Open the activities menu and note each distinct type the map offers, then play one round of each. The tracker commonly lists nine types. Keep a written note of the ones you have tried, because the menu groups similar activities under different icons. Finish with the rarest type while it is still on the map.
trophies.short: Try each type of activity once.

steps.text: Open the activities menu and list every distinct activity type.
Play one full round of each type on the map.
Check the activity screen until all nine types are marked.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold medals, not completions, drive this trophy. Visit every Shooting Range marker and replay a challenge until the score screen shows gold before moving on. The commonly cited target is 42 challenges. Weapon choice is fixed per challenge, so learn the recoil pattern rather than buying upgrades. Each range challenge has a fixed weapon, so learn the recoil pattern on a replay instead of buying upgrades [7].
trophies.short: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge.

steps.text: Visit each Shooting Range marker and note the challenge list.
Replay a challenge until the score screen shows a gold medal.
Continue until all 42 challenges show gold.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win, do not merely finish, at every Top Fun drone-race location. Each marker can be replayed, so a loss only costs a retry. The usual target is 14 locations. Use the course preview to learn the first gate, then fly a clean line instead of chasing raw speed. Keep a note of locations already won so you do not repeat them. The route board shows the gate order before the countdown, so read it once and fly the first two gates cleanly rather than chasing top speed [7].
trophies.short: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location.

steps.text: Open the map filter for Top Fun drone races and mark every location.
Win each race; a finish short of first place does not count.
Replay until all 14 locations are cleared.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Only different race events count, so repeating a favourite circuit will not finish the list. Rotate between street races, drone races and any other event the map labels as a race. Keep a simple checklist of wins by location. Twenty distinct wins is the target, and a second-place finish does not count. The map filter separates street and drone races, so alternate the two types to reach twenty distinct wins faster [7].
trophies.short: Win 20 different races.

steps.text: Filter the map for race events and note their locations.
Win each event rather than simply finishing it.
Win 20 different races without repeating one.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal’s fishing challenge is a one-off world activity, not a story mission. Find the marker, start the challenge and beat Cal’s catch rather than simply finishing. Reeling too early snaps the line, so let the tension meter settle before each pull. If you lose, the challenge can be retried from the same spot. Watch the line-tension meter: let it settle to the neutral band before each pull, then reel in short bursts [5].
trophies.short: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.

steps.text: Find Cal’s fishing challenge among the world activities.
Cast, let the tension settle and beat Cal’s total catch.
Retry from the same marker if the first attempt loses.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Any complete arcade game works; there is no score requirement. Walk up to an arcade cabinet, start a game and play it through to the game-over or credit screen. Avoid quitting to the map mid-run, because the trophy checks the finished state. A short beat-’em-up cabinet is the quickest option. A cabinet in a bar counts even if the high-score table is already full; the check is for reaching the end screen [5].
trophies.short: Complete an arcade game.

steps.text: Find an arcade cabinet in a bar or venue and start a game.
Play through to the game-over or credit screen without quitting.
No score target is needed; finishing is enough.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish every job in Andy’s stranger strand, including the final mission, before the main story reaches its point of no return. The strand is reported to close as the finale approaches, so do it when it first appears rather than saving it for cleanup. Keep a manual save before the last Andy job so a failed objective can be retried without replaying the chain. If a marker disappears, check the other character’s map before assuming it is gone. Andy’s intro job is easy to delay; pin the strand on the map and finish its last job before the Chapter 5 boundary [6].
trophies.short: Complete the final mission in Andy's stranger strand (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Open Andy’s stranger strand when the first marker appears.
Complete every job in the chain, including the final mission.
Do it before the final story mission; the strand can close.

window.locks: Before the final mission; the strand closes as the finale approaches
window.save: Manual save before starting Andy’s last job

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton’s chain is another strand that can close when the finale begins. Work through every job to the final mission as soon as the marker is available. Keep a manual save before the last job so a failed chase can be retried. This trophy is separate from the eight-strand aggregate. Kenton’s marker sits among the Chapter 5 strands; pin it early and finish the last job before the finale trigger [6].
trophies.short: Complete the final mission in Kenton's stranger strand (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Start Kenton’s strand from the stranger marker.
Finish every job through the final mission.
Clear it before the finale; the chain can close.

window.locks: Before the final mission; the strand closes as the finale approaches
window.save: Manual save before starting Kenton’s last job

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy’s strand is time-sensitive in the same way as the other named chains. Complete every job to the final mission before the finale, and do not leave it for post-story cleanup. A manual save before the last job makes a failed objective cheap to retry. The award lands on the final mission’s results screen. Billy’s marker can be easy to miss while other strands are active, so open the map filter and pin it when the intro job appears [6].
trophies.short: Complete the final mission in Billy's stranger strand (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Open Billy’s strand when it appears on the map.
Play every job in the chain to the final mission.
Finish before the finale; the strand can close.

window.locks: Before the final mission; the strand closes as the finale approaches
window.save: Manual save before starting Billy’s last job

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: This is an aggregate trophy: eight complete stranger strands, not eight missions. The named strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone among them) each have their own final job, and the earlier stage trophies already track several of them. Use the map’s stranger markers and finish each chain to its last mission. Because individual strands can close, clear them before the finale even though this aggregate is not separately flagged.
trophies.short: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Use the stranger markers to list every named chain.
Finish each chain through its final mission rather than only its first job.
Complete eight full strands before the finale cleanup.

trophies.conflict: Sources disagree on whether the eight-strand count includes partner strands or only map stranger markers [2][4].

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy’s strand should be finished before the finale, although sources are less specific about the exact cutoff than for the three confirmed chains. Play every job to the final mission and keep a save before the last one. If the marker vanishes, reload an earlier chapter save and finish the chain first. This is marked possible rather than confirmed because the lock is reported, not documented. Randy’s chain is reported to close later than the confirmed strands, but keep the save before the last job because the window is not documented [6][7].
trophies.short: Complete the final mission in Randy's stranger strand (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Find Randy’s first job and follow the chain.
Complete the final Randy mission before the finale.
Keep a manual save in case the marker closes early.

window.locks: Before the final mission; sources report the chain closing after the story
window.save: Manual save before starting Randy’s last job

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone’s strand is another reported late-story lock. Finish every job through the final mission before triggering the finale. The award is separate from the eight-strand aggregate, so a completed Tyrone chain still needs the other strands for that silver. Manual-save before the last job if the objective is a chase. The final Tyrone job is reported to include a chase; start it with a fast car and a clear wanted level so the results screen is not lost [6].
trophies.short: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's stranger strand (time-sensitive).

steps.text: Open Tyrone’s strand from the map marker.
Play the chain through its final mission.
Finish it before the finale and keep a fallback save.

window.locks: Before the final mission; sources report the chain closing after the story
window.save: Manual save before starting Tyrone’s last job

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditation spots are world collectibles, but the map opens in stages and one commonly reported spot sits behind early story access. Visit every marker and hold the meditate prompt until the character finishes the animation; cancelling early may not register. PSNProfiles lists 18 spots, while a community map lists 15, so use the in-game collectible screen as the authority. If a spot is missing, finish the current chapter and check again before assuming it is bugged. The collectible screen lists spots by district; use that list, not a community map total, when the counter stalls [2][7].
trophies.short: Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida.

steps.text: Finish the Chapter 1 story beat that opens the northern map districts before sweeping for spots.
Turn on the meditation-spot filter and work one district at a time.
Start with the earliest spot the filter shows; a reported early spot sits behind story access.
Hold the meditate prompt until the full animation and sound cue finish.
Do not cancel the prompt to save time; an interrupted animation may not register.
After each chapter, reopen the collectible screen for newly revealed spots.
If the counter stalls below 18, compare the in-game list with the 15-spot community map before assuming a bug.

window.locks: Spots open as chapters unlock; a reported early spot is story-gated
window.save: Manual save before a chapter finale if a spot remains

trophies.conflict: PSNProfiles counts 18 meditation spots; a community map counts 15 [2][7].
trophies.unconfirmed: Whether the Chapter 1 balcony spot is required for the trophy is not confirmed by the official description [1][7].

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret’s request is a one-time hunt for a named animal, so treat the first attempt as the only attempt. Take the request when it appears, track the animal with the hunting vision and avoid firing until you have a clean shot. A wounded animal that escapes can fail the request. Manual-save before you start tracking so a bad shot does not cost the strand. Bret’s animal does not respawn after a failed hunt, so reload the pre-track save instead of searching the same area again [6].
trophies.short: Hunt the unique animal for Bret (one-time).

steps.text: Accept Bret’s request when the activity appears.
Use hunting vision to track the named animal and take a clean shot.
If it escapes, reload the save rather than searching the map.

window.locks: Bret’s request is one-time; the unique animal does not respawn
window.save: Manual save before tracking the animal

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Cards are collected in packs, but this trophy checks completed sets rather than total cards. Open the deck screen and note which sets are closest to completion before hunting. Trade duplicates through the game’s card system if a set stalls. Three full sets is the target; a fourth set is wasted effort unless you want the collection.
trophies.short: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets.

steps.text: Open the deck screen and note the sets nearest completion.
Collect or trade the missing cards for those sets.
Complete three full sets and confirm the deck screen.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It points are scattered across the map and each location only counts once. Use the in-game filter to show remaining points and work district by district. The counter is visible on the activity screen, so stop at 100 rather than sweeping the whole state. A short recording or photo at each point is enough; there is no quality score. The activity counter is the authority, not the map icon total; stop at 100 and confirm the upload animation finished at each point [7].
trophies.short: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations.

steps.text: Turn on the WAiNK It map filter and pick a district.
Use the point and let the upload animation finish.
Work district by district until the counter reads 100.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the timed or scored world events on the map, not story missions. Open the challenges board to see the running count and pick events near your current district. Fifty is the target; repeatable challenges may not count twice, so vary the type. Bronze-level clears are enough unless a challenge states otherwise.
trophies.short: Complete 50 Challenges.

steps.text: Open the challenges board and read the remaining event types.
Clear challenges across districts instead of repeating one.
Finish 50 challenges and check the board count.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This needs your partner in the same session and a four-star wanted level that you both lose. Start a chase away from water and tunnels so the escape route stays open. Swap to a fast car before the level reaches four stars, then break line of sight and wait for the meter to cool. Do it while your partner is available; a solo session cannot trigger it. Start the chase inland and keep the partner in the same vehicle; water and tunnels can break the escape line-of-sight check [6].
trophies.short: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner (partner-based).

steps.text: Play with your partner in the same session.
Reach a four-star wanted level and escape together.
Break line of sight and wait for the meter to empty.

window.locks: Requires your partner in the same session
window.save: Manual save before starting the chase

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops back-to-back without letting the wanted level reset, with your partner present. Plan a route through a dense commercial district so the next shop is close, and use the same vehicle to avoid losing the level between stops. The third robbery must complete before you escape. Save before the first shop; a death resets the chain. Pick three shops on the same block; the wanted level must stay live while you move between doors, so do not enter a getaway vehicle early [6].
trophies.short: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner (partner-based).

steps.text: With your partner, pick three shops close together.
Rob them back-to-back without losing the wanted level.
Escape only after the third robbery registers.

window.locks: Requires your partner and an unbroken wanted level
window.save: Manual save before the first robbery

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Vehicle discovery counts when you enter or drive a model you have not yet logged. Work through parking lots, dealerships and highway traffic rather than buying expensive cars. The vehicle list in the pause menu shows what is missing. One hundred distinct models is the target; colour and trim do not create a new entry.
trophies.short: Discover 100 vehicles.

steps.text: Open the vehicle list and note the missing categories.
Enter or drive a new model in each category.
Keep sweeping until 100 distinct vehicles are logged.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus slows time, so the challenge is finding five enemies close enough to kill before it ends. Start the fight in a crowded interior or a gang hideout instead of an open street. Activate Focus only after the first enemy is in view, then move between targets without leaving cover. If the fifth kill lands after Focus ends, the attempt does not count; retry at a denser location.
trophies.short: Take down 5 enemies in one Combat Focus.

steps.text: Start a fight at a dense location such as a gang hideout.
Activate Combat Focus when several enemies are in view.
Score five takedowns before the Focus meter empties.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA is the airport, and the trophy wants a departure the game does not schedule. Reach the airside area, take a plane or helicopter and leave without using a normal flight prompt. The exact trigger is not described officially, so try a runway take-off rather than a taxi or passenger flight. If nothing pops, reload a save and approach from a different gate.
trophies.short: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.

steps.text: Go to VCIA and reach the airside apron.
Take an aircraft and leave without a scheduled flight.
If no award appears, reload and try another gate or runway.

trophies.unconfirmed: The exact “unscheduled departure” trigger is not described officially; runway and stolen-aircraft methods are unverified [1][7].

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a hint rather than an instruction, and no cited source publishes a fixed Rhino spawn. Treat it as an open-world encounter: keep a wanted level high in a wide area and watch for military vehicles, or check the map for a tank-related activity. Do not waste hours at one guessed location. If you see a Rhino, engage it before leaving the area.
trophies.short: Deal with a Rhino tank (the description hints at them).

steps.text: Keep a high wanted level in a wide, open district.
Watch for a Rhino or a tank-related map activity.
If a Rhino appears, engage it before it despawns.

trophies.unconfirmed: No cited source publishes a fixed Rhino location; the guide avoids inventing one [1][7].

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Pick a jewellery store with a back entrance and go in on foot without firing. Knock out or avoid the staff, take the display stock and leave before the alarm completes. Being spotted voids the attempt even if you still escape. A suppressed weapon and a silenced vehicle make the exit much easier.
trophies.short: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.

steps.text: Scout a jewellery store with a back entrance.
Enter quietly and rob the displays without being detected.
Escape before the alarm completes its cycle.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Five bank vaults, each followed by a successful escape. Scout the vault entrance before triggering the robbery so you know the fastest route to a getaway vehicle. The escape counts only when the wanted level is fully lost. Repeating the same vault may not count twice, so spread the robberies across districts. The vault escape only registers when the wanted level is fully clear, so break line of sight before driving to the next district [5].
trophies.short: Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape.

steps.text: Scout five different bank vaults before starting.
Rob each vault and reach a getaway vehicle.
Lose the wanted level completely before moving on.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armoured trucks spawn on the road network, so the reliable method is to wait on a highway and follow one until it stops. Ram or shoot the escort, take the cargo and escape the police. A sticky bomb on the rear doors saves time. If the truck despawns, switch sessions or reload a save rather than chasing a marker that is already gone. Armoured trucks are more common on the highway ring; follow one until it stops rather than firing at speed [5].
trophies.short: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.

steps.text: Wait on a highway and follow an armoured truck.
Stop it, take the cargo and escape the police.
If it despawns, reload instead of chasing the old marker.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Exploration counts named areas, not every square metre of the map. Drive the perimeter roads and enter each district until its name appears on screen. A tracker commonly lists 52 areas. Leave the map filter on to spot unnamed gaps, and use a helicopter for the last few edges rather than walking them.
trophies.short: Explore all of Leonida.

steps.text: Open the map and note every named district you have not entered.
Drive or fly through each district until its name appears.
Finish the last edges by air until all areas are logged.

trophies.conflict: One tracker lists 52 named areas; the in-game map may group districts differently [2][7].

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Each gang owns at least one illegal operation, and the trophy wants one robbery per gang. Use the map’s criminal-activity filter to find operations, then note which gang controls each before attacking. Nine is the commonly cited count. A stealth approach keeps the escape short, but the trophy only checks the robbery and escape. The criminal-activity filter names the controlling gang, so note the gang before attacking and avoid repeating the same operation [7].
trophies.short: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.

steps.text: Filter the map for illegal operations and identify each gang.
Rob one operation controlled by each gang.
Escape and confirm the count after each robbery.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: This is a location-and-action trophy: Ocean Beach, a bar with a view and a cocktail. Go to the beachfront at dusk for the clearest view, order the drink and let the animation finish. The exact bar is not named in the official description, so try the seafront venues rather than an inland cocktail bar. If the prompt is missing, change the time of day. The seafront bars share the same prompt; changing the time of day is the reliable reset if the cocktail animation does not trigger [7].
trophies.short: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.

steps.text: Go to Ocean Beach and find a seafront bar with outdoor seating.
Order a cocktail and let the full animation play.
If no prompt appears, change the time of day and try another venue.

trophies.unconfirmed: The official description does not name the bar; the seafront location is not independently confirmed [1][3].

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Find a vehicle showroom with glass frontage, get into a display car and drive through the window. The smash must happen from inside the showroom, not by ramming the building from the street. Pick a car with enough acceleration to clear the frame, then escape the resulting wanted level. A failed smash can be retried at another showroom.
trophies.short: Smash out of a vehicle showroom.

steps.text: Find a vehicle showroom with a street-facing window.
Get into a display car and accelerate through the glass.
Escape the wanted level after the smash.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Kolt & Associates runs the bowling alley named in the description. Start a full game and bowl every frame through to the final score screen. Quitting after a few frames will not count. Use the lane guide to keep the ball straight; the trophy does not require a high score, only a completed game. The lane screen accepts a full game even at a low score; the trigger is the final frame, so do not leave after the tenth frame [5].
trophies.short: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.

steps.text: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a full game and bowl every frame.
Let the final score screen appear before leaving.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This is a hidden partnership trophy with a deliberately vague description. Play the main story and the partner activities together rather than treating them as optional side content. The trigger is not documented, so keep a save before major partnership missions and let the scenes play out. If it has not appeared by the finale, replay the partner missions from the pause menu.
trophies.short: A hidden partnership trophy with a deliberately vague description.

steps.text: Play the main story and partner activities together.
Let partnership cutscenes and optional conversations finish.
If it is still missing, replay partner missions from the pause menu.

trophies.unconfirmed: The exact partnership trigger is not documented; only the official description is available [1][3].

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices are recorded throughout the story and world content, and the commonly cited target is 500 decisions. You do not need to track each one manually: keep playing and choose dialogue options instead of skipping them. A second playthrough can fill a stubborn remainder. The official description does not publish the number, so treat 500 as tracker guidance rather than gospel.
trophies.short: A hidden choices trophy; PSN tracks up to 500 choices.

steps.text: Make dialogue and story choices instead of skipping conversations.
Keep playing both story and world content to add decisions.
Use a second playthrough if the tracker still shows a gap.

trophies.unconfirmed: The 500-choice figure comes from a tracker, not the official description [2].

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The wording points to succeeding on a second attempt after a failure. Try a world event, let it fail once, then retry the same event and finish it. Do not reload between attempts, because the retry has to happen in the same session. The exact event is not named, so pick a repeatable activity rather than a story mission.
trophies.short: A hidden second-attempt trophy.

steps.text: Pick a repeatable world event and intentionally fail once.
Retry the same event in the same session and complete it.
Avoid reloading between the failure and the retry.

trophies.unconfirmed: The exact event and retry window are not described officially [1][7].

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This is a mystery-event trophy, and the official description gives no location. Explore the odd roadside and wilderness markers at night, interact with anything that does not match a normal activity, and let the scene finish. Datamined locations circulate online but are not confirmed here. Keep a manual save before investigating so a scripted failure can be undone.
trophies.short: A hidden mystery-event trophy.

steps.text: Explore odd roadside and wilderness markers at night.
Interact with anything that does not match a normal activity.
Let the full scene play and keep a save before investigating.

trophies.unconfirmed: The trigger and location are not described officially; circulating map pins are unverified [1][7].

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A melee drive-by means attacking a pedestrian from a moving vehicle, not running them over. Drive slowly alongside a target, trigger the melee attack and knock them down. A motorcycle or open-top car makes the animation easier to see. Do it away from a police station to avoid a chase interrupting the attempt. Use an open-top vehicle or motorcycle so the melee animation is visible; a closed car can make the prompt fail [5].
trophies.short: Bowl someone over with a melee drive-by.

steps.text: Drive slowly alongside a pedestrian in an open vehicle.
Trigger the melee attack rather than running them over.
Leave the area before the police respond.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are a laundering activity, so the money has to pass through your contacts rather than sit in your wallet. Complete the marked-bills jobs as they appear and keep laundering until the cumulative total reaches $250,000. The activity screen tracks the amount. There is no time limit; smaller jobs add up. The contact’s laundering screen shows the running total; smaller jobs still count, so clear them between story missions instead of waiting for one large payout [5].
trophies.short: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills.

steps.text: Complete marked-bills jobs and deliver the cash to a contact.
Keep laundering in the marked-bills activity screen.
Repeat until the cumulative total reaches $250,000.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spending counts across weapons, clothes, vehicle and service shops, so do not funnel everything into one store. Buy useful upgrades first, then fill the remainder with clothing or vehicle parts. The total is cumulative and the pause menu shows your spending. One hundred thousand dollars is the target; property purchases may not count.
trophies.short: Spend $100,000 across all shops.

steps.text: Buy useful weapon and vehicle upgrades first.
Fill the remainder across clothing and service shops.
Check the pause-menu spending total until it reaches $100,000.

trophies.unconfirmed: Whether property purchases count toward the $100,000 total is not stated officially [1][7].

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Garage properties are bought from the in-game property website, not found as collectibles. Open the property list, sort by garage capacity and buy the cheapest unowned garage first. Eight properties is the commonly cited total. Keep enough cash for the final purchase before starting the sweep, because some garages unlock only after story progress. The property site lists garage capacity as well as price; a cheap garage still counts toward the eight, so buy by capacity first [7].
trophies.short: Purchase all garage properties.

steps.text: Open the property website and list every garage for sale.
Buy the cheapest unowned garage first and work upward.
Keep enough cash for the final purchase and confirm all eight.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: The Scooter Bros app registers vehicles you own or find, and the trophy checks ten distinct registrations. Open the app after every new vehicle and register it before selling or storing it. Scooters are the obvious choice, but the app may accept other small vehicles. If a registration does not stick, reopen the app and sync the list. The app keeps a separate list from your garage, so register a scooter immediately after purchase and check the counter before selling it [7].
trophies.short: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.

steps.text: Open the Scooter Bros app after acquiring a new vehicle.
Register each distinct vehicle before selling or storing it.
Keep going until ten registrations are listed.
